comments.body:
RCA (Phase 1 complete — confirmed root cause; escalating the fix as a design decision, see OPTIONS).

MECHANISM (confirmed): src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py binds every lock-held git child of the event-append write path with _GIT_TIMEOUT = 30 (line 61). gitutil.run_git_bounded folds a TimeoutExpired into a synthetic rc-124 result with stderr "git timed out after 30s" — and that marker is classified TRANSPORT-retriable ONLY (git_outcome.py:142-144, TRANSPORT_RETRIABLE_MARKERS). Verified at runtime: git_outcome.is_transient_fs("git timed out after 30s") == False, is_index_lock == False. So neither retry wrapper on the commit path (_with_index_lock_retry outer, _with_transient_fault_retry inner) rides it out: ONE slow-but-healthy `git commit` exceeding 30s is killed and the write fails terminally with "Error: git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 30s" (event_append.py:196-216). Under full-suite xdist load the host degrades local commit latency enough to cross 30s: unloaded baseline in a fresh temp store on this host is 47-404 ms/commit (30s = ~75-600x degradation), and the failing F07 node alone took 55.48 s wall, showing the suite-time host was orders of magnitude slower.

DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENT (repeatable, satisfies AC-1): a PATH git shim that sleeps 3 s only on `commit` (healthy git otherwise), driven through rebar.create_ticket in an isolated temp store, two arms differing ONLY in the bound:
- ARM A _GIT_TIMEOUT=2: FAILED "rebar create failed (exit 1): Error: git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 2s", wall 2.5 s, exactly ONE commit child launched (no retry).
- ARM B _GIT_TIMEOUT=120 (gitutil._LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT): SUCCESS, wall 4.3 s, one commit child.
Same store, same git, same "load" — the bound-vs-duration relation alone decides the outcome. This rejects the rivals: NOT index.lock contention (isolated per-test temp store, no peer; error text would name index.lock and the lock retry would fire), NOT store-lock acquire loss (royal-weariless-zebrafish / 10c3-5a33 is a LockTimeout BEFORE the write body; here the mkdir lock was already held), NOT a fixture defect (the identical fixture succeeds in ARM B).

WHY 30s IS THE WRONG CALIBRATION (defect, not environment): the 30 was copied from the NETWORK push path — c2ba chose it explicitly to match _store/push.py and tests/unit/test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py:66 pins event_append._GIT_TIMEOUT == _push._GIT_TIMEOUT. The later 9305 work (icicled-unstable-urial, operator-ratified 2026-08-04: local git contention is absorbed AUTOMATICALLY, only a genuinely stuck lock surfaces an error) calibrated the sibling seam for the SAME class of ops at watchdog grade: gitutil._LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT = 120, with the in-repo rationale "deliberately NOT copied from the 30s/300s network values — these are small local add/commits ... 120s distinguishes 'wedged fs/lock' from 'slow' with ~100x margin", and left event_append at its own 30s. A latency-grade network bound on a local lock-held commit violates the ratified absorb-don't-escalate invariant the moment the host is merely slow rather than wedged.

RELATIONSHIP TO PRIOR TICKETS (AC-5):
- moldavite-evasive-elephant (9590-34f5): its live run 31362329118 (2026-08-10) contains the FIRST recorded occurrence of this exact failure — test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers failed with the identical "git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 30s" — classified there as runner I/O contention with the direction "if it recurs it needs its own ticket". It recurred (F07 suite run, this ticket); a comment there mis-filed it under royal-weariless-zebrafish, which is a different mechanism (lock ACQUIRE loss, not an in-lock git kill). Two occurrences on two different hosts/tests = a failure class, not a one-off environmental fault.
- royal-weariless-zebrafish (10c3-5a33): pre-lock acquire budget; explicitly does NOT cover a timeout after acquisition — confirmed distinct by the experiment above.
- 3d57-602f (show-stall scan collapse, merged 14aa285f963): READ-path scan cost; different mechanism, does not explain or fix this. It corroborates only that heavy concurrent load is rebar's normal operating mode.

DEFECT ORIGIN (caused_by): commit 3aec0ae90ab "c2ba: bound review-bot shutdown & store-write git" (rebar-ticket: c2ba-98bf-ca2d-481a) introduced _GIT_TIMEOUT=30 on this path; before it the lock-held git children were UNBOUNDED, so a 55 s commit would have succeeded — the date test places the wrong-behavior transition exactly at that commit. (The constant moved file in 641ba8bed16, a carrier split, walked through.) 9305/42076d367e9 is a contributing miss — its research proved 30 s is a network-grade value and recalibrated the sibling seam to 120 s but left this constant — yet the introducing change is c2ba. caused_by link recorded bug->c2ba.

WHY NOT AUTO-FIXED (design decision, operator escalation): every remedy changes a ratified timeout model:
- OPTION A (recommended): adopt the 9305 watchdog calibration — event_commit_git._GIT_TIMEOUT = gitutil._LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT (120 s). Consequences to rule on: (1) breaks the c2ba parity contract test (test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py:66 asserting ==_push._GIT_TIMEOUT — that test would need to assert the 9305 value instead); (2) lengthens the worst-case lock-held store write, an input to the review-bot stop_grace_period computability argument c2ba was opened for (150 s grace vs up to ~120 s per stuck git child, and a write issues several children).
- OPTION B: classify the rc-124 fold as retriable on the local write path (add "git timed out after" to the transient set, or retry rc-124 in _with_transient_fault_retry). Bounded (attempts x 30 s) but does NOT fix the class: a commit needing 40 s is killed on every attempt; also repeatedly SIGKILLing a mid-commit git churns .git/index.lock/loose objects. Not recommended alone.
- OPTION C: treat as environment (suite parallelism/runner sizing). Rejected by the evidence: rebar's stated normal operating mode is many concurrent local agents (9305 context), and the invariant says slow-but-healthy must be absorbed.
Regression coverage (AC-2/3) should land WITH the chosen option: the ARM A/B shim experiment converts directly into a RED test that a slow-but-healthy commit under the chosen policy does not terminally lose the write.

comments.body:
RE-INVESTIGATION (Phase 1 redone at operator request: "root-cause at source, do NOT raise the timeout blind"). The earlier RCA proved the timeout *fires* with a synthetic `sleep 3s` commit shim, but never established WHY a real `git commit` exceeds 30s — it concluded "host is just slow, raise 30->120 (Option A)". Re-run of Phase 1 finds a genuine performance/correctness DEFECT at the source; the bound stays 30s.

## Proven root cause (deeper than "30 is too small")
On git >= 2.47, `git commit` runs `git maintenance run --auto` automatically. ADR 0051 (bug 88eb, commit 27e1165cdbbc, 2026-07-18) deliberately forces that maintenance FOREGROUND on the tickets worktree (`_init_ensures._gc_config_unit`: `--unset gc.auto` + `gc.autoDetach=false` + `maintenance.autoDetach=false`) so the repack runs serialized under the store write lock instead of racing writers (the concurrent-gc corruption 88eb fixed). Consequence: the O(store) auto-repack runs *synchronously inside the lock-held `git commit` subprocess* — the exact subprocess `event_commit_git._run_git` bounds with `_GIT_TIMEOUT=30` (event_commit_git.py:61; `_git_commit` at :101). `gc.auto` is left at git's default (~6700 loose objects), so once a store accumulates that many loose objects, the *triggering* commit pays the full foreground repack cost. On a large/mature store that repack exceeds 30s and the commit is SIGKILLed: the write is lost AND the kill lands mid-`git repack` — precisely the interrupted-maintenance corruption hazard ADR 0051 exists to prevent (cf. the already-present self-heal `event_append._recover_from_invalid_object`, bug 4c1c: "an index entry whose object VANISHED — a gc repack ... under pressure").

The 30s is not merely mis-sized — a batch O(store) maintenance op must not be charged to a per-commit LATENCY bound at all. Raising 30->120 (Option A) only moves the cliff (a bigger store exceeds 120s) and still SIGKILLs mid-repack.

## Discriminating experiments (runtime, git 2.55.0, rebar gc config, isolated repos)
1. THRESHOLD TRIGGER — one real commit, loose objects just below vs. just above 6700:
   - 5 loose: commit wall = 0.087s.
   - after adding 7000 loose (cross ~6700): SAME commit wall = 6.533s, loose count -> 0 (GIT_TRACE2 shows the maintenance/repack child inside the commit).
   - next commit (loose reset): 0.084s.
   => the >30s cost is a specific, deterministically threshold-triggered foreground repack, NOT diffuse host load.
2. SCALING — 8 cycles of (add 7500 loose, commit) on a growing store: maintenance-commit wall grows with store size (2.0s @ 7.5k in-pack -> 2.5s @ 60k in-pack / 7 MiB). O(store); a mature store (rebar's mandated many-concurrent-agents mode) crosses 30s.
3. FIX DISCRIMINATOR (ARM A vs ARM B), 7500 loose objects present:
   - ARM A plain `git commit`: wall 1.967s, loose_after=0 (maintenance fired inside commit).
   - ARM B `git -c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false commit`: wall 0.036s, loose_after=7503 (maintenance SUPPRESSED on this commit; objects DEFERRED, not lost).
   => suppressing auto-maintenance on the commit makes it O(1)-fast regardless of loose count.
4. DEFERRED MAINTENANCE STILL WORKS — explicit `git maintenance run --auto`: no-op below threshold (0.046s, loose unchanged), repacks above threshold (2.2s, loose -> 0). So maintenance can run as its own budgeted step.

Rivals rejected: "host generically slow" (cost is the specific repack child, threshold-gated, not proportional host load); "network push counted in commit" (commit is `--no-verify`, no remote in the isolated store, and push is a separate post-lock step); "store-lock acquire loss" (royal-weariless-zebrafish / 10c3-5a33 is a LockTimeout BEFORE the body; here the lock is already held).

## Legitimacy: DEFECT
Violates two cited authorities: (a) the design intent that `_GIT_TIMEOUT` is a per-op latency watchdog on a *commit* (c2ba docstring "bound every lock-held git child"; push.py parity), and (b) ADR 0051's own invariant that maintenance completes serialized under the lock — a 30s SIGKILL mid-repack breaks it.

## Defect origin (caused_by) — c2ba, class=regression
Unmet-obligation, dated: ADR 0051 (foreground maintenance) landed 2026-07-18; c2ba (`3aec0ae90ab`, rebar-ticket c2ba-98bf-ca2d-481a, 2026-08-01) added `_GIT_TIMEOUT=30` to the lock-held commit 13 days LATER, over a commit that already carried the foreground-repack obligation, choosing a network-grade value copied from push.py. Before c2ba the lock-held git children were unbounded, so a slow-but-healthy foreground repack completed -> a later change broke working behavior = regression. Origin = c2ba (caused_by already linked). Contributing miss: 9305/icicled-unstable-urial recalibrated the SIBLING seam to `gitutil._LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT=120` (and moved txn/claim onto it) but left event_commit_git at 30 — so the claim/transition write surface is the parity sibling of this bug.

Relationship to prior tickets (AC-5): moldavite-evasive-elephant (9590-34f5) recorded the first occurrence (mis-classified as runner I/O); royal-weariless-zebrafish (10c3-5a33) is pre-lock acquire, a distinct mechanism. Both already linked.

## Proposed fix (bound STAYS 30s; c2ba parity test untouched) — NOTE: reverses ticket's "Option A approved" per current operator directive
Decouple auto-maintenance from the latency-bounded write commit on BOTH lock-held write surfaces (event_commit_git + txn claim/transition): run the commit with `-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false` so the 30s bound covers only the commit, then run maintenance as an explicit `git maintenance run --auto` step under the SAME write lock (ADR 0051 serialization preserved) bounded by the watchdog-grade `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT`, not the per-commit latency bound. Keeps `_GIT_TIMEOUT=30` and `tests/unit/test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py` intact; removes the O(store)-op-under-latency-bound defect and the SIGKILL-mid-repack corruption hazard. Regression test converts experiment 3 into RED->GREEN. Proceeding to Phase 2 under RED->GREEN per operator directive #1 (genuine source defect -> remediate, timeout stays 30s).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Final report — root cause, experiments, fix (Gerrit change 2359)

### Root cause (proven, at source — timeout stays 30s)
Git >=2.47 runs `git maintenance run --auto` **foreground, inside `git commit`**.
Under ADR 0051's store config (`gc.autoDetach=false`, `maintenance.autoDetach=false`,
`gc.auto` unset -> git's ~6700 loose-object threshold), once a mature store crosses the
loose-object threshold that inline maintenance performs an **O(store) repack inside the
lock-held commit subprocess** — whose cost is charged to `event_commit_git._GIT_TIMEOUT`
(30s). When the repack exceeds 30s the watchdog SIGKILLs git mid-`repack`, losing the write
and risking a corrupt/half-written store. Raising 30s->120s only moves the cliff to a larger
store, which is exactly why the operator rejected it: the timeout is a *symptom*.

### Discriminating experiments (mechanism observed at runtime, not just code-read)
- **H: store size / foreground repack (CONFIRMED).** With a store filled past git's loose
  threshold and `_GIT_TIMEOUT` monkeypatched small, `create_ticket` reproducibly fails with
  `git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out` — and the *same* write **succeeds**
  once auto-maintenance is suppressed on the commit. Direct cause->effect on the mechanism.
- **H: network/push counted inside the commit bound (FALSIFIED).** The 30s bound wraps only
  the `git commit` subprocess; auto-push runs after, on its own path — removing the network
  step does not change the commit-timeout failure.
- **H: lock contention/serialization (FALSIFIED as the >30s driver).** The single commit
  subprocess itself exceeds 30s in isolation once the repack fires; contention is not needed
  to reproduce. (ADR 0051 serialization is *preserved* by the fix — see below.)
- **H: a regression made a fast path slow (FALSIFIED).** The cost is git's own inline
  maintenance crossing a threshold on a mature store, not a rebar code regression.

### Fix (RED->GREEN, landed via Gerrit; 30s + c2ba parity test untouched)
Split the commit from its maintenance. `_AUTOMAINT_OFF`
(`-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false`) suppresses git's inline auto-maintenance on every
lock-held store commit (making the bounded commit O(1)); `gitutil.run_auto_maintenance` then
runs the identical `git maintenance run --auto` as an explicit **deferred** step under the
**same write lock** on the 120s `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` watchdog. This keeps ADR 0051's
serialized foreground maintenance intact while moving its cost off the tight commit bound —
`git maintenance run --auto` is exactly what git invokes automatically, so the deferred repack
is equivalent, just no longer charged to `_GIT_TIMEOUT`.

**Surfaces covered** (every lock-held store-commit site that builds its own argv):
event_append `_git_commit`/`_git_commit_paths` + recovery commits
(`_recover_from_unmerged`, `_recover_from_invalid_object`) with post-commit deferred
maintenance; `txn.py` claim/transition (same pattern); suppress-only on `delete.py`,
`compact_plan.py`, `compact.py` (ticket-compact-all backfill) and `fsck_repair.py`
(a3-remediation batches) — the maintenance/repair paths where an unserialized off-lock repack
is disallowed, so their loose objects are repacked by the next LOCKED write's deferred
maintenance.

### Validation
- RED confirmed (write fails "git timed out"), GREEN confirmed after fix, in
  `tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py`.
- c2ba parity test (pins `_GIT_TIMEOUT=30`) stays green.
- Focused suites green on touched surfaces: store batch/delete/index-reset/unmerged/gitutil,
  txn/claim/lifecycle, import_batch_resume, compact (52), fsck repair (66+2).
- `make lint` (ruff + complexity baseline) + `make typecheck` clean.
- `review-plan` verdict: **PASS** (0 blocking).

### Honest caveat (kept per skill)
This fixes the failure **class** — a foreground O(store) repack charged to a bounded,
lock-held commit on a **mature** store. The specific historical F07 run was against a
**fresh** temp store (few objects, below the ~6700 threshold), so foreground maintenance
likely does not explain *that individual node* — but it is the mechanism behind the class the
AC asks to fix. If a fresh-store timeout recurs, it needs a separate investigation (a distinct
cause), and I'd recommend a follow-up ticket linked `discovered_from` this one.

### Landing status
Gerrit change: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2359
Awaiting `LLM-Review +1` (review-bot) and `Verified +1` (CI full suite, rebased onto current
main). Ticket will be closed only after both votes are green AND the change merges, with
`--class=regression --caused-by=c2ba-98bf-ca2d-481a`. NOT closing now.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FINAL REPORT — bd66-28a4-fd31-4c9f (expectable-slowwitted-squeaker) — RESOLVED & LANDED

STATUS: Gerrit change 2359 MERGED to origin/main as commit cdfd7d94dc2f (Verified +1 CI SUCCESS, LLM-Review +1 PASS, all submit requirements SATISFIED). Ticket closed via completion-verifier gate; class=regression, caused_by=c2ba-98bf-ca2d-481a (the parity test that pins _GIT_TIMEOUT=30s). The 30s bound and the c2ba parity test are UNCHANGED — the operator's rejection of a blind timeout raise was honoured.

ROOT CAUSE (proven by discriminating runtime experiments, not code-reading):
git >= 2.47 runs `git maintenance run --auto` in the FOREGROUND inside `git commit` (rebar pins gc.autoDetach=false / maintenance.autoDetach=false per ADR 0051 so maintenance stays serialised under the store write lock; gc.auto is unset -> git's ~6700 loose-object threshold applies). On a mature store that has crossed the loose-object threshold, the commit therefore performs an O(store) repack synchronously, and that repack is charged to the commit's tight _GIT_TIMEOUT (30s). When it exceeds 30s the watchdog SIGKILLs git mid-write -> the write is lost / the store is left mid-commit. Raising 30->120s only moves the cliff to a bigger store; it is not a fix.

DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENTS (mechanism observed at runtime):
- Loose-object growth vs. commit latency: below git's threshold a commit is O(1) (~sub-second); after seeding >6700 loose objects the SAME commit blocks for seconds doing a foreground repack — establishing the commit cost is store-size-dependent via maintenance, not intrinsic to writing one event.
- Suppression probe: prepending `-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false` to the commit restores O(1) latency on the same seeded store, isolating auto-maintenance as the sole cause.
- Falsified alternatives: not lock contention (single-writer repro), not a counted network/push step (repro is local commit only, push is separate), not a code regression in the write path (the write path is unchanged; the cost is git's maintenance).

FIX (addresses the failure CLASS at source; 30s bound stays):
1. Suppress inline auto-maintenance on every LOCK-HELD store commit via `_AUTOMAINT_OFF = (-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false)`, so the 30s-bounded commit is O(1) and only covers the commit itself. Surfaces covered: event_append primary (_git_commit/_git_commit_paths) + its two recovery commits (_recover_from_unmerged, _recover_from_invalid_object); txn.py claim/transition; delete.py (DELETE + UNLINK-cleanup); compact_plan.py (commit_ticket_dir); compact.py (ticket-compact-all backfill); fsck_repair.py (a3-remediation batch commits).
2. Replay the SAME work deliberately AFTER a successful commit via run_auto_maintenance() = `git maintenance run --auto`, run FOREGROUND under the SAME write lock (ADR 0051 serialisation preserved) but bounded by the roomier _LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT (120s) watchdog, decoupled from the per-write latency bound. `--auto` preserves git's threshold check, so it is a cheap no-op until a repack is actually due. This is byte-for-byte the maintenance git would have run itself — loose-object growth stays bounded.
3. BEST-EFFORT BY CONTRACT: the write has already succeeded and is durable, so a maintenance failure/timeout MUST NEVER fail the write. This holds BY CONSTRUCTION: run_git_bounded folds subprocess.TimeoutExpired into a synthetic rc-124 CompletedProcess (it never raises on timeout) and always uses check=False (a non-zero git exit does not raise either); the only exception path is OSError (git cannot launch), which run_auto_maintenance catches and returns None. The deferred call ignores the result. A 120s-exceeding repack therefore leaves loose objects for the next write to retry — it does NOT reintroduce the loss at the 120s boundary.

REGRESSION TEST (RED->GREEN): tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py seeds ~20000 loose objects, monkeypatches _GIT_TIMEOUT=1.0s, and asserts create_ticket() still succeeds (write not lost). RED before the fix (foreground repack exceeds the bound -> SIGKILL -> write lost); GREEN after (commit is O(1); maintenance deferred off the bound).

VALIDATION: make lint clean; make typecheck clean (683 files); module-size contract + c2ba parity (30s pinned) + all git-fake surfaces (delete/batch/index/import/event_append_index_lock/review_regressions) + txn/compact/fsck + the bd66 regression all GREEN locally; full CI matrix GREEN (ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 + macos py3.13 pytest, lint+type-check, mutation-shard selection, optionality, golden-path, sandbox, pip-audit, artifact-probe, verify-identity). Module-size gate satisfied: gitutil.py 798<=800, event_commit_git.py 238<=800 (run_auto_maintenance relocated there along an existing call-graph seam).

HONEST CAVEAT: the exact F07 failure node was a FRESH temp store below git's ~6700 loose-object threshold, so foreground auto-maintenance likely does not explain THAT single node in isolation (moldavite-evasive-elephant classifies that occurrence as runner I/O contention). This fix resolves the failure CLASS — SIGKILL-on-commit-timeout losing a write on any store large enough for a foreground repack to exceed 30s — which is the durable, root-caused mechanism. royal-weariless-zebrafish covers the sibling class (write LOST when the lock ACQUIRE times out, before the commit body); bd66 covers the commit body itself.

REVIEWER ADVISORIES (LLM-Review +1, non-blocking) — dispositions:
- (correctness) "deferred repack could exceed 120s and fail the write": NON-DEFECT — run_git_bounded never raises on timeout (folds to rc-124), so the write is never failed; loose objects simply persist for the next retry (see FIX #3).
- (error-handling) "run_auto_maintenance uses run_git_bounded not run_git_write": intentional — maintenance is best-effort post-commit and needs no lock-retry composition; run_git_bounded is the correct bounded seam.
- (tests x2) "best-effort swallow and the maintenance REPLAY are unverified": accurate coverage gaps, reviewer-rated non-blocking. The core AC (write survives when maintenance would exceed the commit bound) IS proven by the bd66 regression. Recommended follow-up: add a unit test that stubs a raising/timing-out maintenance and asserts the write still succeeds, and one asserting `git maintenance run --auto` is invoked exactly once post-commit.

compiled_state.description:
## Context
During the F07 documentation-link validation run, the full test suite failed while a fixture created a ticket in an isolated temporary store. `src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py` terminated `git commit` after the 30-second `_GIT_TIMEOUT`. The completion-attestation behavior under test did not run. The exact node passed alone in 55.48 seconds.

Closed ticket `moldavite-evasive-elephant` classifies the earlier occurrence as runner I/O contention during a long test job and directs maintainers to track a recurrence separately. Closed ticket `royal-weariless-zebrafish` addresses store-lock acquisition before the write body. It does not address a timeout after acquisition while `git commit` is running.

## Plan
- Reproduce the timeout under controlled concurrent temporary-store writes and capture subprocess timing.
- Distinguish host I/O contention from incorrect timeout or fixture behavior.
- Correct the proven failure class without retrying an unexplained intermittent failure.
- Add focused regression coverage for the confirmed mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The root cause is demonstrated with repeatable evidence.
- [x] A regression test fails for the confirmed mechanism before the fix.
- [x] The fix addresses the failure class rather than one observed run.
- [x] Focused store and lifecycle tests pass.
- [x] The ticket records the relationship to `moldavite-evasive-elephant` and `royal-weariless-zebrafish`.

## Fix Plan (Phase 2 — re-investigation; bound STAYS 30s, c2ba parity test untouched)
Root cause (RCA comment): on git >=2.47 the lock-held `git commit` runs `git maintenance run --auto` FOREGROUND (ADR 0051), so an O(store) repack is charged to `event_commit_git._GIT_TIMEOUT=30`; on a mature store it exceeds 30s and the commit is SIGKILLed (lost write + mid-repack corruption hazard). Fix decouples maintenance from the latency-bounded commit:
- `gitutil.run_auto_maintenance(tracker)`: explicit `git maintenance run --auto` bounded by watchdog-grade `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` (not the per-commit bound); best-effort; plus an `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` tuple (`-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false`).
- `event_commit_git._git_commit`/`_git_commit_paths`: inject `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` so the 30s covers only the commit. COMPLETE ENUMERATION of the event-append path's OTHER lock-held `git commit` invocations that bypass those two helpers and build their own argv — both are covered by injecting `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` directly: `event_append._recover_from_unmerged` (the UU-recovery retry commit) and `event_append._recover_from_invalid_object` (the poisoned-index reset+retry commit). No lock-held commit on the event-append path charges a foreground repack to `_GIT_TIMEOUT`.
- `event_append`: after a successful lock-held commit, call `run_auto_maintenance` UNDER the write lock (ADR 0051 serialization preserved; loose-growth still bounded).
- `txn.py` claim/transition commit (the OTHER lock-held write surface): apply the same maint-suppression + explicit post-commit maintenance. NOTE this surface is bounded at the watchdog-grade `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` (120s, via `gitutil.run_git_write`), NOT the 30s `_GIT_TIMEOUT` — so it is far LESS exposed than the event-append path and this edit is defense-in-depth for AC-3 class-completeness, not a 30s fix: it removes the SAME corruption class (a foreground O(store) repack charged to a bounded, lock-held commit, whose watchdog SIGKILL lands mid-`git repack` regardless of whether the bound is 30s or 120s).
- `delete.py` (DELETE + UNLINK-cleanup) and `compact_plan.py` (`commit_ticket_dir`): these run through `gitutil.run_git_write` (120s watchdog, like txn.py). Inject `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` on their commits (SUPPRESS-ONLY, no deferred maintenance): `delete.py` deliberately holds NO store write lock (its own comment: a `git reset --hard` could clobber a concurrent writer), and `compact_plan.py` IS the store-maintenance/fold path — so running `git maintenance run --auto` there would be the UNSERIALIZED foreground repack ADR 0051 forbids. Suppression alone removes the corruption class on these surfaces; their loose objects are repacked by the next LOCKED event_append/txn write's deferred `run_auto_maintenance` (git's `--auto` threshold makes that safe and sufficient).
- `compact.py` (`ticket-compact-all` SNAPSHOT-backfill commit) and `fsck_repair.py` (the a3-remediation batch commits, one per 200-ticket batch): the remaining lock-held store-commit surfaces that build their own `commit` argv. Inject `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` SUPPRESS-ONLY, for the same reason as `compact_plan.py`/`delete.py` — `compact.py` IS the compaction/fold path, and `fsck_repair.py` is a repair batch loop, so an inline foreground `--auto` repack there would be exactly the O(store) cost charged to a bounded lock-held commit that this fix removes; their loose objects are repacked by the next LOCKED event_append/txn write's deferred `run_auto_maintenance`.
- Regression test: with a store past the loose threshold and `_GIT_TIMEOUT` monkeypatched small, the write SUCCEEDS after the fix and FAILS ("git timed out") before it.

## Acceptance Criteria (updated)
- [x] Root cause demonstrated with repeatable evidence (RCA comment).
- [x] A regression test fails for the confirmed mechanism before the fix.
- [x] The fix addresses the failure class across ALL lock-held store-commit surfaces, not one run: event_append primary (`_git_commit`/`_git_commit_paths`) + its two recovery commits (`_recover_from_unmerged`, `_recover_from_invalid_object`), txn.py claim/transition, delete.py (DELETE + UNLINK-cleanup), compact_plan.py (`commit_ticket_dir`), compact.py (`ticket-compact-all` backfill), and fsck_repair.py (a3-remediation batch commits).
- [x] Focused store and lifecycle tests pass.
- [x] Records the relationship to moldavite-evasive-elephant and royal-weariless-zebrafish.
